Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Sanjay Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Anit Kumar Shukla, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.
Applicants seek bail in Case No. 4344 of 2010, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act, Police Station Bharthana, District Etawah, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants has argued that the applicants are absolutely innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR was instituted in the year 2004 against the applicants and other family members nine in all.

The police was pleased to file a closure report in Dinesh And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132286413/
1 the said case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the basis of protest petition, the applicant and other co-accused persons were summoned in the year 2007 but the informant appeared before the court concerned and stated that he had not filed any protest petition whatsoever, as such the court concerned was pleased to proceed against him who challenged the said order by filing a petition under section 482 Cr.P.C. before this Court and the proceedings were stayed.
5.
Learned counsel has further argued that the said petition has been disposed of in the year 2021.
Subsequent to it, non-bailable warrants were issued against the applicants on 09.10.2024.
All the three applicants are the brother-in-law (jeth) of the deceased person.
They have themselves surrendered before the court concerned on 09.12.2024.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicants to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against them.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicants have also been touched upon at length.
7. There is no criminal history of the applicants.
The applicants are languishing in jail since 09.12.2024 and they are ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicants are released on bail,
they will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicants have made out a case for bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicants- Dinesh, Shivraj and Ashok, who are involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicants shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicants shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicants is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against them in accordance with law.
11. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
